svg.text: A2. The planet stored, with polar ice
Picture A again, with an ice cap on each pole: a continent under an ice sheet in the south, broken sea ice in the north. Seed 7.
N
ocean
plains
forest
desert
mountains
ice sheet
sea ice
city
town
looking down on each pole, 45 degrees across
North: sea, no land
A pack of sea ice, broken into floes. Near
the pole the floes are big and close
together. Toward the edge they shrink, part,
and thin to scattered bergs in open water.
South: a continent under ice
A dome of ice sheet over land, with bare
rock breaking through it. A flat ice shelf
around the coast, then an ocean ring with
the odd berg.
Dashed rings are 15 and 30 degrees from the pole. The south disc is mirrored as if seen from outside the planet.
How the ice is made (nothing stored)
It is part of the same function as the rest of the planet: the latitude (the y of the point), the sea (open water is below zero) and our noise.
Sea ice (north): the pack is thick near the pole and thins to nothing at about 28 degrees of it. Floes are cells of a cellular noise; the chance a
cell is ice, and how much of it, falls with the pack's thickness.
Ice sheet (south): a land mask about 24 degrees across, noisy at its edge; the ice dome rises inward; where it is high and a second noise is high,
rock shows through.
Nothing here is a table: the same seed gives the same ice. Cities and towns are kept out of the caps.
